issues.legal_issue: Protection for a pre-constitutional law placed in the constitutional schedule extends to a challenge based on a property right under the repealed constitutional statute that was carried into the fundamental-rights chapter.
material_facts: The challenged acquisition law was enacted before the Constitution and was later placed in the constitutional schedule.
The challenge alleged that the law’s compensation provisions violated the property guarantee in the repealed Government of India Act, 1935.
That guarantee was substantially carried into the fundamental-rights chapter of the Constitution.
issues.conclusion: The protection attached to the scheduled law barred a challenge based on the repealed property guarantee, as well as a challenge based on the corresponding fundamental right.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-B protects a scheduled enactment or its provisions from being held void for inconsistency with, or taking away or abridging, rights in Part III. Section 299 of the Government of India Act, 1935 was in substance a fundamental right carried into Part III, so Article 31-B protection extends to a challenge based on that repealed provision. The Court relied on Dhirubha Devisingh Gohil v. State of Bombay and State of Uttar Pradesh v. H.H. Maharaja Brijendra Singh, and distinguished N.B. Jeejeebhoy v. Assistant Collector because the law there lacked Article 31-B protection.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_preconstitut: A party in a constitutional challenge asks a court to invalidate a law enacted before the Constitution.
predicates.law_is_in_protected_schedule: The challenged law has been placed in the constitutional schedule that confers immunity from fundamental-rights challenges.
predicates.challenge_relies_on_transferred_property: The party relies on a property guarantee from a repealed constitutional enactment that was substantially carried into the Constitution’s fundamental-rights chapter.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge to a pre-constitutional law relies on a transferred property right and the law is in the protected schedule, the challenge is barred by scheduled-law immunity.

issues.legal_issue: The statutory limits on compensation for land acquired for resettlement of displaced persons are valid.
material_facts: Land was acquired for resettlement purposes under a special acquisition law.

The compensation provisions directed the arbitrator to have regard to the ordinary land-acquisition compensation principles, subject to provisions that could cap compensation by reference to an earlier market value with an addition or, for qualifying purchases, by reference to the purchase price.
The acquisition law was placed in the constitutional schedule.
issues.conclusion: Both provisos to the compensation provision are valid, and the appeals challenging them were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31-B immunizes a scheduled law and its provisions from a challenge alleging violation of rights in Part III, including the substantially corresponding property guarantee in section 299 of the Government of India Act, 1935. The Court applied Dhirubha Devisingh Gohil v. State of Bombay and State of Uttar Pradesh v. H.H. Maharaja Brijendra Singh; it also agreed with the Full Bench decision in Union of India v. Smt. Mohinder Kaur. Once Article 31-B applies, the Court does not examine whether the statutory valuation principles are relevant or whether the resulting compensation is illusory.

predicates.appeal_from_land_acquisition_compensatio: A party appeals from an award determining compensation for acquired land.
predicates.compensation_provisions_are_challenged_o: The party argues that statutory compensation limits violate a constitutional property guarantee.
predicates.acquisition_law_is_in_protected_schedule: The law under which the land was acquired has been placed in the constitutional schedule that confers immunity from fundamental-rights challenges.

issues.definition: If an appeal from a land-acquisition compensation award challenges the compensation provisions on property-rights grounds and the acquisition law is in the protected schedule, those provisions are valid.

issues.legal_issue: A compensation cap tied to market value before a period of wartime price escalation is not arbitrary when the selected date has a real connection to the acquisition law’s objective.
material_facts: The compensation formula used the lower of the market value at the acquisition-notice date and an earlier market value increased by a fixed percentage.
The earlier valuation date immediately preceded the Second World War, and the Court noted that the war situation contributed to land-price escalation.
The acquisition law was enacted to facilitate land acquisition for resettling displaced persons at a reasonable price.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the earlier valuation date was relevant to the statutory objective and could not be struck down as arbitrary.
issues.legal_principle: A statutory date used in determining compensation is not arbitrary where it has a real nexus to the law’s objective. The Court relied on the historical circumstance that the Second World War contributed to land-price escalation. It added that, because the acquisition law was protected by Article 31-B, it was unnecessary to examine in depth whether the valuation principles were otherwise relevant to land valuation.

predicates.appeal_from_land_acquisition_compensatio: A party appeals from an award determining compensation for acquired land.
predicates.compensation_cap_uses_earlier_market_val: The compensation formula limits the award by reference to market value at a date earlier than the acquisition.
predicates.earlier_date_precedes_wartime_price_esca: The earlier valuation date falls before a period in which wartime conditions contributed to increased land prices.
predicates.date_has_nexus_to_resettlement_objective: The selected valuation date is connected to the objective of acquiring land for resettlement at a reasonable price.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a compensation cap based on earlier market value, and that date precedes wartime price escalation while remaining connected to the resettlement objective, the date is not arbitrary.
